If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to hedge downside risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.49) and forecast is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% to mid-horizon (8–14 days) to align with momentum bias.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, subtract 0.3–0.7% from mid-horizon (8–14 days) to avoid overcorrection.

In late horizon (15–30 days), if sentiment is positive, apply +0.2–0.5% to forecast to reflect sustained bullishness; if negative, apply -0.2–0.5% to reflect consolidation or reversal.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, apply +1.0–1.5% to forecast at 7–10 day horizon to capture reversal momentum.
